purpose: Curated confusable passage negatives on corpus v3 for retrieval regression checks; a case passes only when evidence ranks above its named decoys. Curated by reading passage text, not tuned to any retriever.

cases.query: What was Berkshire's total insurance float at the end of 2009?
cases.rationale: 2009 letter states float of $62 billion; the 2010 and 2008 letters give $66 billion and $58.5 billion.

cases.query: How large was Berkshire's float at the end of 2006, before the Equitas contract?
cases.rationale: 2006 letter gives $50.9 billion; the 2005 float-growth passage reads the same but says $49 billion.

cases.query: How large had Berkshire's total float grown to by 2021 since it entered insurance?
cases.rationale: 2021 letter says $147 billion; 2020 letter discusses $138 billion of float.

cases.query: What underwriting loss did Berkshire incur in 1999 and what float cost resulted?
cases.rationale: 1999: $1.4 billion loss, 5.8% cost; 2000: $1.6 billion loss, 6% cost.

cases.query: How much did Berkshire's insurance float grow in 2002 and what did using it cost?
cases.rationale: 2002 float rose $5.7 billion to $41.2 billion at 1% cost; 2004 passages give other float figures.

cases.query: By how much did Berkshire's float rise in 2012?
cases.rationale: 2012 letter reports a $2.5 billion increase; 2016 letter shows the same float table with later numbers.

cases.query: How much did Berkshire's insurance float increase during 2022 with the help of an acquisition?
cases.rationale: 2022 float went from $147 billion to $164 billion; the 2021 letter describes the earlier float.

cases.query: What did Buffett mean by Berkshire's derivatives float at yearend 2008?
cases.rationale: Derivatives float (payments received less losses paid) differs from insurance float in the same letter.

cases.query: How must purchased Goodwill be amortized under the accounting rules, and is the charge tax deductible?
cases.rationale: Accounting amortization over 40 years versus the economic Goodwill passage.

cases.query: What creates economic Goodwill in a business, as opposed to the Goodwill account on the balance sheet?
cases.rationale: Economic Goodwill is excess return on tangible assets; neighbours define the accounting item.

cases.query: How does Buffett define owner earnings and why do they differ from reported GAAP earnings?
cases.rationale: Owner earnings (earnings plus non-cash charges less maintenance capex) versus look-through earnings.

cases.query: What is retroactive reinsurance and how is it treated under GAAP in Berkshire's earnings?
cases.rationale: Retroactive insurance covering past events versus a rule proposed to apply retroactively.

cases.query: What did Berkshire include in and exclude from its operating earnings figure in 1977?
cases.rationale: 1977 definition excludes realized capital gains; later passages reuse the term in look-through context.

cases.query: How does the annual goodwill amortization charge widen the gap between intrinsic value and book value?
cases.rationale: 1999 letter ties the roughly $500 million charge to the book-value gap; 1983 explains economic Goodwill.

cases.query: What were See's Candies sales and pre-tax profits in 2006?
cases.rationale: Sales $383 million and pre-tax $82 million; other years give $83 million and cumulative totals.

cases.query: What were sales at the Nebraska Furniture Mart in 1990?
cases.rationale: 1990: $159 million; 1993 gives $200 million and 1986 gives $132 million.

cases.query: How much were See's pre-tax operating earnings in 1977?
cases.rationale: 1977: $12.6 million; 1991 passage also starts from the 1972 figure of $4.2 million but ends at $42.4 million.

cases.query: What combined ratio did National Indemnity's traditional business post in 1996?
cases.rationale: 1996: 74.2; 1995: 84.2, same sentence structure.

cases.query: How much float had Ajit Jain's reinsurance business built by the 2011 letter?
cases.rationale: 2011: $34 billion; 2012: $35 billion; 2010: $30 billion.

cases.query: What were Berkshire's operating earnings in 2023?
cases.rationale: 2023: $37.4 billion; the 2022 letter gives the record $30.8 billion.

cases.query: What was Berkshire's book value per share at yearend 1979?
cases.rationale: 1979: $335.85; 1981 letter gives $526.02 with the same $19.46 starting point.

cases.query: How did Lou Simpson's equity portfolio at GEICO perform against the S&P 500 in 1996?
cases.rationale: Lou Simpson at GEICO versus the later managers Combs and Weschler beating the S&P.

cases.query: How is performance pay split between Todd Combs and Ted Weschler?
cases.rationale: 80% own results and 20% partner's; the 2010 passage covers Combs's pay versus the S&P only.

cases.query: Why did Rose Blumkin (Mrs. B) leave the Nebraska Furniture Mart in 1989?
cases.rationale: 1989 departure after family disagreement; 1993 passage tells her life story and store sales.

cases.query: How did Don Wurster's National Indemnity traditional business do in 1995?
cases.rationale: National Indemnity traditional versus Ajit Jain's reinsurance division.

cases.query: How did GEICO's float and underwriting do in 2001 under Tony Nicely?
cases.rationale: GEICO versus Berkshire's smaller primary insurers in the same letter.

cases.query: How much float does General Re hold according to the 2007 letter?
cases.rationale: General Re $23 billion versus NICO $950 million float.

cases.query: What is Ben Graham's Mr. Market allegory about market quotations?
cases.rationale: Explanation of the allegory versus passing remarks that Mr. Market was a friend or will offer chances.

cases.query: What did Ben Graham teach Buffett about the difference between price and value?
cases.rationale: The price/value quote versus a biographical mention of Graham's class.

cases.query: What is Graham's saying about the market as a voting machine and a weighing machine?
cases.rationale: The quote itself versus another passage that merely credits Graham's teaching.

cases.query: How does GEICO's cost advantage work as a moat around the castle?
cases.rationale: 1986 explains the moat concept with expense ratios; 1995 only says the moat widened.

cases.query: What did Buffett say about Ajit Jain's reinsurance float and underwriting profits in 2002?
cases.rationale: Substantive float figures versus the 'bow deeply' flourish next to smaller-insurer results.

cases.query: What does widening the moat mean in practice for Berkshire's operating managers?
cases.rationale: Explanation of the practice versus praise of managers as brilliant at it.

cases.query: From 1995 through 2018, how far did GEICO's float grow?
cases.rationale: 2018 letter gives $2.5 billion to $22.1 billion; other years cover partial spans.

cases.query: How did Nebraska Furniture Mart's sales change over the ten years ending 1986?
cases.rationale: 1986 letter compares $44 million with $132 million.

cases.query: How much has See's earned pre-tax in total since Berkshire bought it, as of the 2011 letter?
cases.rationale: $1.65 billion in 2011 versus $1.9 billion in 2014 and $857 million in 1999.

cases.query: How large were the portfolios run by Todd Combs and Ted Weschler by 2013?
cases.rationale: 2013: each exceeds $7 billion; 2011: $1.75 billion at cost.

cases.query: What level of look-through earnings did Buffett say was needed by 2000 to meet the 15% goal, as stated in the 1992 letter?
cases.rationale: 1992 letter: $1.8 billion; 1993 and 1994 raise it to $1.85 billion.

cases.query: At the time of the 1972 purchase, what were See's sales and pre-tax earnings?
cases.rationale: Price $25 million, sales $30 million, earnings under $5 million; other passages give 1972 earnings only.

cases.query: How much had Coca-Cola's annual dividend to Berkshire grown by 2022 compared with 1994?
cases.rationale: 2022: $75 million to $704 million; 2010 letter gives $88 million (1995) to $376 million (2011).
